mathematical_results.claim: For the standard 14641 class, C≅C(4); p∈{1,2,4}
Exist period-2 and period-4 AS-regular Z-algebras and a flat family with period-1 special and generic period 2
Marked 4-periodic quadratic Z-algebra presentations with dim V=4 dim R=6 are equivalent to four Grassmannian factors modulo GL4^4
Periodic shift s iff all integer-index degree-one isomorphisms preserve R_i; no periodicity of the gauge relative to a chosen tau4 assumed
1-periodic Z-algebras with selected isomorphism correspond to graded algebras; forgetting yields coarser equivalence
For p=1 or 2, a chosen 4-period sigma4 equal to a (4/p)-power of a p-period induces compatible p-periodic diagonal four-window data, and conversely

Frobenius/Nakayama 4-periodicity on the quadratic dual from any two top traces differs by diagonal vertex conjugacy; canonical-marked and unmarked standard ASZ4 have the same geometric isomorphism classes
On the canonical four-window, canonical marking is equivalent to four trace-pairing matrix equalities P_i^T=Q_i with nonzero traces
Frobenius property of quadratic dual in strict four-window can be certified from degrees 0..5 and complementary multiplication pairing ranks, not sufficient for Koszulity
For canonical Frobenius four-window, an unmarked period p exists iff 4 invertible maps g_i satisfy (g_i⊗g_{i+1})R_i=R_{i+p}; hence periods 1/2/4 are finite orbital solvability tests
A(lambda)(1)=A(-lambda) strictly, while A(lambda) is not isomorphic to A(-lambda) for every parameter with minimal period 2 (in particular lambda=1)
Polynomial 4-space exterior dual trace alternating (-1)^i normalizes Nakayama to strict period4; exact Python check passed

mathematical_results.limitations: Does not classify all AS-regular points or make the polynomial system computationally easy
